checks.claim: Key: energy is the ability to do work or cause change
checks.note: TeachEngineering (grades 3-5): 'the ability to do work, to make things happen and to cause changes'. Grokipedia Energy: 'the capacity of a physical system to perform work' (https://grokipedia.com/page/Energy).

checks.claim: Wrong choice 'A push or a pull that acts on an object' is a force, not energy
checks.note: Grokipedia Force: 'a force is a push or pull upon an object'; Grokipedia Energy contrasts energy (scalar) with force, 'a vector quantity describing the push or pull on an object'.

checks.claim: Wrong choice 'A fuel that is burned to give off heat': fuel is matter that stores energy, not energy itself
checks.note: EIA: chemical energy is energy stored in the bonds of atoms and molecules (in coal, petroleum, biomass); the fuel is the store, not the energy.

checks.claim: Wrong choice 'A kind of matter that takes up space' is wrong (energy is not matter)
checks.note: Energy is a scalar quantity, a property of a system, not a substance.

checks.claim: Stem: six forms named in grade 5 classes (light, heat, sound, electrical, chemical, mechanical) = Florida SC.5.P.10.1
checks.note: CPALMS pages do not render for the fetcher (JavaScript shell / 404), but a web search for the exact phrase 'basic forms of energy, including light, heat, sound, electrical, chemical, and mechanical' with 'SC.5.P.10.1' returns the CPALMS standard page (Standard #: SC.5.P.10.1) and Leon County Schools' SC.5.P.10.1 document as matches, so the wording is the benchmark's, not only the flashcard site's.

checks.claim: Context: fuels such as wood and coal are matter that stores energy
Key: a battery stores its energy as chemical energy
checks.note: Grokipedia: a battery is 'designed to convert stored chemical energy into electrical energy through oxidation-reduction reactions'; it never says a battery stores electricity.

checks.claim: Wrong choice 'Electrical energy' is wrong for a battery at rest (the M1 misconception)
checks.note: The stored form is chemical; electrical energy is the output when a circuit is closed. Not defensible at grade 5 (a capacitor, not a battery, stores electrical energy).

checks.claim: Wrong choices 'Light energy' and 'Thermal energy' are wrong
checks.note: EIA lists batteries as stores of chemical energy.

checks.claim: Context: only when switched on does the battery change chemical into electrical energy, which flows through the wires to the bulb
checks.note: Matches the TEKS 5.8A flashlight chain (chemical to electrical to light). Grokipedia: the voltage 'drives current when connected to an external circuit'.

checks.claim: Grade note: TEKS 5.8A uses the flashlight battery example
checks.note: Search results (Kesler poster, TEA energy-transfer PDF https://tea.texas.gov/academics/subject-areas/science/tif-energy-transfer.pdf) give 5.8A as energy transformation in systems with the flashlight battery, chemical to electrical to light.

checks.claim: Key: a bulb changes electrical energy into light and heat
checks.note: Incandescent: 'over 90% of input electrical energy dissipates as heat ... with less than 10% converted to visible light'. TeachEngineering: a bulb left on is 'electrical energy changing into heat energy ... as well as producing light'.

checks.claim: Wrong choice 'Only light' is wrong (every bulb gives some heat)
checks.note: ENERGY STAR: LEDs 'use heat sinks to absorb the heat produced by the LED'; even LEDs make heat.

checks.claim: Wrong choice 'Light and sound' is wrong
checks.note: Grokipedia notes incandescents work 'without flicker or audible hum' (fluorescents can buzz, but a flashlight bulb is incandescent or LED). Not defensible.

checks.claim: Wrong choice 'Light and electricity' is wrong (electricity is the input, not an output form)
Context: an old-style bulb with a glowing wire turns most of its energy into heat
checks.note: Filament heated by current until it glows; over 90% becomes heat. Energy.gov (via search): incandescents release about 90% of their energy as heat.

checks.claim: Context: a modern LED wastes far less but still warms up
checks.note: ENERGY STAR: thermal management is 'the single most important factor' in an LED's life; LEDs need heat sinks.

checks.claim: Key: a fan's motor changes electrical energy into motion
checks.note: Grokipedia: a motor converts 'electrical energy into mechanical energy'; fans are a listed application. True whether the fan is plugged in or battery-run: the motor's own change is electrical to motion.

checks.claim: Wrong choice 'Motion into electrical energy' is a generator, not a motor
checks.note: Grokipedia: a generator 'converts mechanical energy into electrical energy'; a motor works the other way.

checks.claim: Wrong choice 'Thermal energy into motion' is a heat engine
checks.note: A heat engine 'converts thermal energy extracted from a hot reservoir into mechanical work'; an electric motor does not.

checks.claim: Wrong choice 'Chemical energy into motion' is a car engine / the body
Context: a car's engine turns the chemical energy in gasoline into motion
checks.note: EIA: 'A car engine burns gasoline, converting the chemical energy in gasoline into mechanical energy.'

checks.claim: Context: mechanical energy is the energy of motion (grade 5 usage)
checks.note: Physics: mechanical = kinetic (motion) + potential (position). Note EIA Kids splits 'motion energy' from 'mechanical energy' (stored by tension); the question survives either way since the key says 'motion'.

checks.claim: Key: the speaker changes electrical energy into sound
checks.note: Grokipedia: the current makes 'the voice coil to move back and forth, vibrating an attached diaphragm or cone'; a loudspeaker converts an electrical audio signal into sound.

checks.claim: Wrong choice 'The microphone' does the opposite (sound into electrical signal)
checks.note: Grokipedia: 'a transducer that converts acoustic sound waves into corresponding electrical signals'.

checks.claim: Wrong choice 'The battery' supplies electrical energy (from chemical), makes no sound
Wrong choice 'The screen' changes electrical energy into light, not sound
checks.note: OLED materials 'produce light when an electric current passes through them'. Edge case for awareness, not an error: a few phones (LG G8 ThinQ 'Crystal Sound OLED', 2019; Samsung's 'Sound on Display' demo; the first Xiaomi Mi Mix) had no earpiece and vibrated the screen with an exciter behind it to carry the caller's voice (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LG_G8_ThinQ, https://www.gsmarena.com/samsung_will_tuck_the_speaker_into_the_display_as_it_did_with_the_selfie_camera-news-34848.php). Even there the exciter is a speaker driver, so 'The speaker' stays the one right answer; if a reviewer wants zero exposure, 'The camera' is an airtight swap.

checks.claim: Stem: inside a phone the caller's voice is an electrical signal
checks.note: The call arrives as radio waves; inside, the audio drives the speaker as an electrical signal (the stem's 'inside a phone' keeps it true).

checks.claim: Context: a speaker makes a small cone shake back and forth very fast
checks.note: True of speakers generally ('diaphragm or cone'). A phone's tiny speaker usually has a flat or domed membrane rather than a true cone; optional polish: 'a thin cone or sheet'.

checks.claim: Context: the battery supplies electrical energy and the screen changes it into light
Key: a solar panel changes light into electrical energy
checks.note: Absorbed photons create electron-hole pairs that the p-n junction separates into a voltage; the conversion does not run through a heat step. EIA: 'Solar photovoltaic cells change radiant energy from the sun into electrical energy' (https://www.eia.gov/kids/what-is-energy/laws-of-energy.php).

checks.claim: Wrong choice 'Heat into electrical energy' is wrong for rooftop panels that run lamps
checks.note: Heat is a loss, not the input (excess photon energy is lost as heat). Solar thermal collectors on roofs heat water and do not run lamps; heat-driven solar power plants are not roof panels. Not defensible in the stem's situation.

checks.claim: Wrong choice 'Chemical energy into electrical energy' is a battery
Wrong choice 'Electrical energy into light' is the reverse (a lamp or LED)
Context: a panel works a little worse when hot
checks.note: Crystalline silicon loses about 0.3 to 0.5% of output per degree C above the 25 C rating (EnergySage gives -0.24 to -0.29%/C for some brands: https://www.energysage.com/solar/solar-panel-temperature-overheating/). 'A little worse' is accurate.

checks.claim: Context: a cold, bright day suits it well
checks.note: A cooler cell is more efficient (negative temperature coefficient). 'Suits it well' is true; the line does not claim winter gives the most total power (shorter days), so it is safe.

checks.claim: Key: nearly all the energy in wind and coal first came from the Sun
checks.note: CK-12: 'Almost all energy comes from the Sun.'; 'The Sun heats some areas more than others, which causes wind.'; 'Fossil fuels are made of the remains of plants and animals that stored the Sun's energy millions of years ago.' The claim is made only for wind and coal, both truly solar in origin; nuclear, geothermal and tidal energy (the real exceptions) are not claimed as solar.

checks.claim: Wind is driven by uneven solar heating
checks.note: Grokipedia: uneven solar heating makes the pressure differences that move air. EIA Kids: 'Wind energy from uneven heating from the sun' (https://www.eia.gov/kids/what-is-energy/sources-of-energy.php).

checks.claim: Coal's energy is ancient sunlight stored by plants
checks.note: EIA: 'Coal contains the energy stored by plants that lived hundreds of millions of years ago in swampy forests'; EIA glossary: photosynthesis runs 'with sunlight as the energy source' (https://www.eia.gov/tools/glossary/index.php?id=Photosynthesis). Burial heat and pressure turned the plants into coal but did not supply its stored chemical energy.

checks.claim: Wrong choice 'The Moon' is wrong (the Moon's pull raises tides, not wind; moonlight is reflected sunlight)
checks.note: Tides come from the Moon's and Sun's differential gravity; tidal energy is not in wind or coal.

checks.claim: Wrong choice 'Earth's hot core' is wrong (geothermal heat is not the energy in wind or coal)
checks.note: CK-12: 'Earth's internal heat does not depend on the Sun for energy' (heat of formation and radioactive decay). It is a real non-solar source, but it is not where wind's or coal's energy came from, so the choice stays wrong.

checks.claim: Wrong choice 'Earth's spinning' is wrong (Coriolis only bends wind)
checks.note: Grokipedia: the Coriolis effect deflects winds 'without altering their speed'; it does no work on the air. (Earth's spin does feed tidal energy, but tides are not in the stem.)

checks.claim: Context: Earth's inner heat and the Moon's pull on the tides are real energy sources too, but tiny beside the Sun
checks.note: Geothermal 0.087 W/m2 and tidal about 0.001 W/m2 against about 239 W/m2 of absorbed sunlight: under 0.04%. PBS NOVA: geothermal is 'the naturally occurring heat coming from Earth's core', tides 'caused by the moon's gravitational pull' (https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/nova/labs/lab/energy/2/1). The Sun also raises part of the tide, but 'the Moon's pull on the tides' is not false.

checks.claim: Key: rushing water's mechanical energy turns the wheels
checks.note: USGS: water falls 'through the penstock', a turbine 'turned by the moving water'; 'A hydraulic turbine converts the energy of flowing water into mechanical energy.' Moving water's kinetic energy is mechanical energy in physics; Kesler's 5th-grade lesson lists 'flowing water' as moving mechanical energy (https://keslerscience.com/describe-energy-transformations-lesson-plan-teks-5.8a).

checks.claim: Wrong choice 'Electrical energy' is wrong (the water holds no electricity; the generator makes it)
checks.note: Potential energy becomes kinetic energy 'which turbines extract'; the turbines drive generators that produce electricity.

checks.claim: Wrong choices 'Chemical energy' and 'Thermal energy' are wrong
checks.note: The water's warmth and chemistry do not turn the turbine.

checks.claim: Stem: water rushes through huge pipes (penstocks) and spins giant wheels (turbines)
checks.note: 'channeling water through penstocks to spin turbines'.

checks.claim: Context: turbines drive generators that change mechanical energy into electrical energy
checks.note: 'A hydroelectric generator converts this mechanical energy into electricity.'

checks.claim: Grade note: SC.5.P.10.1 names mechanical energy among the basic forms
checks.note: Benchmark wording confirmed through search indexing of the CPALMS page (the page itself does not render for the fetcher).

checks.claim: Key: a sandwich (food) holds chemical energy
checks.note: Kesler (TEKS 5.8A): 'Chemical energy is stored in batteries, food, fuel, and wood', and it uses a sandwich as its own example. Grokipedia Chemical energy: food, coal and petroleum 'store vast amounts of chemical energy' (https://grokipedia.com/page/Chemical_energy).

checks.claim: Wrong choice 'A wound-up spring' holds mechanical (elastic) energy, not chemical
checks.note: EIA: 'Mechanical energy is energy stored in objects by tension', with compressed springs and stretched rubber bands as examples. Kesler: a compressed spring stores mechanical energy.

checks.claim: Wrong choice 'A stone warmed by a fire' holds thermal energy
checks.note: 'Thermal energy, or heat, is the energy that comes from atoms and molecules moving in a substance.'

checks.claim: Wrong choice 'A ringing bell' gives off sound energy
checks.note: Kesler: 'Sound energy is vibrations spreading through the air'. (A vibrating bell also has mechanical energy, but in no reading does it hold chemical energy, so the key is unique; the context's 'gives off sound energy' is the accurate phrasing.)

checks.claim: Context: the body releases food's chemical energy to move and to keep warm
checks.note: Respiration oxidises glucose 'to release stored chemical energy as heat and ATP'; ATP drives muscle movement. EIA: energy not used for work is released as heat (https://www.eia.gov/kids/what-is-energy/laws-of-energy.php).

checks.claim: Context: wood, coal, gasoline and batteries store chemical energy too
checks.note: Burning wood or gasoline releases chemical energy stored in bonds; batteries and fossil fuels named as chemical-energy sources.

unit_notes: All 9 questions pass. No key or wrong choice was found false, and no quotations or myths appear in player text. Checks of the points flagged in the brief: (1) The Sun question claims solar origin only for wind and coal, both truly solar; none of its wrong choices is a real source of either (geothermal = 'Earth's hot core' and the Moon are true non-solar sources but not of wind or coal; Earth's spin does no work on wind), and the context names geothermal and tides as real but tiny (under 0.04% of absorbed sunlight). (2) Coal's energy is plants' stored sunlight (EIA Coal explained + EIA photosynthesis glossary + CK-12). (3) The solar panel turns light, not heat, into electricity; heat lowers output about 0.3-0.5% per degree C. (4) Every chain (battery chemical, bulb light + heat, motor electrical to motion, generator the reverse, heat engine, car engine, speaker / microphone, PV) checks out. SC.5.P.10.1: CPALMS pages are a JavaScript shell to the fetcher (Preview pages empty, Export pages 404), but a search for the exact benchmark phrase with the code returns the CPALMS standard page and Leon County Schools' SC.5.P.10.1 document, so the writer's quotation is the benchmark's wording. Minor, optional: (a) phone question, 'The screen' has a rare exception (LG G8 ThinQ's Crystal Sound OLED used the screen as the earpiece via an exciter); the key still stands; swap to 'The camera' only if wanted. (b) Phone speakers have flat or domed membranes; 'a small cone' could read 'a thin cone or sheet'. (c) Non-player grade notes for the fan and speaker questions cite 'the curriculum line for TEKS 5.8A'; the TEKS that names electrical energy into motion and sound is 5.8B (a grade 5 unit plan quotes 5.8B as electrical energy in complete circuits transformed into motion, light, sound, or thermal energy). The map line G5.P5 is tagged 5.8A, so the note matches the map; worth retagging G5.P5 with 5.8B too.
